title: Pulley wheel revision: correct top pocket radius and depth from caliper measurements
description:
Second design pass for the Lamona LAM8652 pulley wheel. Supersedes the geometry of design issue openscad-ycm (do NOT overwrite its outputs - new issue id means new filenames per AGENTS.md File Naming).

Job folder: source/lamona_pulley_wheel/ (spec: requirements.md)

== NEW HARD MEASUREMENTS FROM PAUL (calipers on the original broken part) ==
These supersede all photo-derived estimates from both cad-designer and cad-critic.

1. ARM TIP DIAMETER = 19.98mm  => arm tip radius 9.99mm.
   Paul said 'radius' but confirmed he meant DIAMETER (IMG_0973 shows the jaws spanning the whole wheel; a 19.98 radius is impossible against a 21.67 OD).
   The arm tips and the pocket outer wall are at the same radius.
   => TOP FLANGE RING WIDTH = (21.67 - 19.98)/2 = 0.845mm.
   Model openscad-ycm had pocket_or = 7.835 (Ø15.67) and a 3.0mm flange ring. Both wrong.

2. POCKET DEPTH = 4.48mm, measured from the TOP FLANGE FACE down to the POCKET FLOOR (Paul confirmed the datum explicitly; IMG_0977).
   => pocket floor sits at z = 6.5 - 4.48 = 2.02mm above the bottom face.
   => solid web beneath the pocket is only ~2.02mm thick.
   Model openscad-ycm floored the pocket at z=1.5 (5.0mm deep) - close, but derived for the wrong reason.

== WHAT THIS DOES TO THE PREVIOUS REVIEW ==
cad-critic (openscad-ca8) finding 1 (pocket radius too small, flange too wide) is CONFIRMED and was in fact understated.
cad-critic finding 2 (pocket is shallow, ~2.0-2.2mm over a ~4.4mm web) is WRONG - it had the pocket/web split inverted. The pocket is DEEP (4.48) over a THIN web (2.02).
The orchestrator's earlier reconciliation on openscad-d3l is therefore also wrong and has been corrected there.

== THE GEOMETRY PROBLEM TO SOLVE - this is the core of this issue ==
A pocket outer wall at r=9.99 with a floor at z=2.02 appears to CLASH with the groove. In the openscad-ycm geometry the groove root is at r=8.635 centred near the mid-plane; at z=2.02 the groove has already cut inward to roughly r=9.1. A plain cylindrical pocket wall at r=9.99 would break through into the groove.

The real part evidently resolves this somehow. DO NOT invent a resolution - work it out from the new broken cross-section photos, and state what you concluded and what evidence supports it:
- images/IMG_0974.png, IMG_0975.png, IMG_0976.png - broken cross-section fragments showing internal structure
- images/IMG_0973.png - arm tip diameter measurement
- images/IMG_0977.png - pocket depth measurement
Candidate explanations worth testing against the photos (not conclusions): the pocket floor may ramp or step upward toward the rim rather than being flat (Paul originally described these as 'wedge' shaped); the pocket outer wall may be tapered rather than cylindrical; the groove may sit lower and/or have a different profile than modelled. If the geometry genuinely cannot close, say so and report it rather than fudging it.

== PRINTABILITY CONCERN TO ADDRESS ==
A 0.845mm top flange ring is almost exactly two perimeters at a 0.4mm nozzle, and it sits directly above the groove. The 2.02mm web is also thin. Assess whether this prints and holds up under sustained cord tension in a warm damp dishwasher door, and say so plainly if faithfulness to the original and printability genuinely conflict here - that is a human decision, not yours to silently trade away.

== CONFIRMED CORRECT - CARRY OVER UNCHANGED ==
OD 21.67, hub boss Ø10.30, bore Ø6.04, hub height 7.88, wheel thickness 6.5, groove depth 2.20, six arms at 60deg, bottom features as PROTRUDING bosses, cord NOT flush (stands ~0.95mm proud - Paul confirmed, openscad-so3 closed).
Bore handling unchanged: bore_d=6.04 plus bore_print_comp=0.30. Stud will not be measured (openscad-vim) - accepted risk, parametric reprint.

== ALSO FIX IF THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS IT ==
- openscad-03d (P2): groove centre sits ~0.55-0.6mm BELOW the wheel mid-plane on the real part (critic measured top flange ~2.05, groove 3.63, bottom lip ~0.90 off IMG_0968). Model has it symmetric. Check against the cross-section photos now available.
- openscad-ajg (P3): spoke ribs measure ~0.7-1.0mm on the real part vs spoke_t=1.30 in the model; and the six spokes punch through the hub boss top chamfer leaving square tabs where the real hub rim is a clean circle.

== DELIVERABLES ==
output/lamona_pulley_wheel-<this-issue-id>.scad and .stl, plus renders (3/4 from above showing pockets/arms/groove, and an underside). No .step. Read printer.yaml. Keep it fully parametric. ONE implementation pass - do not iterate autonomously. Do not close this issue.
design:
POCKET FLOOR GEOMETRY: the pocket FLOOR IS FLAT. Apparent depth varies only because the TOP surface steps down from the raised axle boss (z=7.88) at the centre to the outer flange face (z=6.5) at the rim - which is what Paul meant by 'the pocket is narrower at the edge, as the central hub is raised'. One flat floor, two datums.
Authoritative values are in the NOTES field (web_t = 2.20 is the driven parameter; depths derived).

=== THE GEOMETRY DOES NOT OBVIOUSLY CLOSE - THIS IS THE CORE TASK ===
Using the openscad-ycm groove (2.2mm deep, root r=8.635, torus arc r=1.75, centred on the mid-plane z=3.25), the groove profile at the pocket wall radius r=9.99 spans z=1.55 to 4.96. A flat pocket floor at z=2.20 sits INSIDE that span, so the pocket would open into the groove.
Pushing the groove down per openscad-03d (centre ~0.55 lower, z_c~2.70) gives a span of roughly z=1.00 to 4.41 at r=9.99 - the floor is still inside it. Off-centring alone does NOT resolve the clash.

Candidates to test against the broken cross-section photos IMG_0974/0975/0976 - these are HYPOTHESES, not conclusions:
1. cad-critic finding 4 (openscad-ca8): the real groove is a V with a radiused root, measurably NARROWER than the modelled half-round (~2.2mm wide at half depth vs 3.25 modelled). A V has far less vertical extent at r=9.99 than a torus does. Most promising lead.
2. Combined with the off-centre groove of openscad-03d.
3. The pocket outer wall tapering inward as it descends rather than being cylindrical.
4. Plain measurement spread - see MEASUREMENT CONFIDENCE below.

cad-critic findings 3 and 4 were logged as 'moderate' and 'low confidence' cosmetic items. In light of the caliper work they are PROMOTED: the groove's true profile and axial position may be exactly what makes the part geometrically possible. Treat them as primary evidence, not polish.

If after working the cross-sections the measurements still cannot all be satisfied at once, STOP and report which pair is mutually impossible. Do not fudge a dimension to make it close.

=== MEASUREMENT CONFIDENCE (Paul, 2026-10-28) ===
Paul spot-checked the same features at different positions around the part and gets slightly different readings each time. His read: the moulding is not perfectly uniform, and the part has been deformed by load in service.

That is almost certainly right. The original is moulded POM (>POM< marking), 20+ years old, held under sustained cord tension, and the surviving piece is broken - so expect as-moulded shrink/draft variation, creep, wear in the groove where the cord runs, and possible distortion near the fracture.

CONSEQUENCES - apply these:
1. STOP TREATING SINGLE READINGS AS EXACT. Quoting 0.01mm off a hand-held caliper on a crept, broken moulding is false precision. Prefer sensible round nominals over chasing the last 0.05mm.
2. THE CLASH MAY NOT BE REAL. The apparent impossibility is of the order of a few tenths of a millimetre. A +/-0.2mm spread could account for all of it. Test whether the geometry closes ANYWHERE within a plausible tolerance band before declaring it impossible - and if it closes, report with how much margin.
3. PRIORITISE BY FUNCTION, NOT FIDELITY. Where measurements conflict, favour the functional dimension.
   FUNCTIONALLY CRITICAL: bore (must spin freely on the stud), groove profile and depth (must retain and release a 3.15mm cord without pinching or throwing it), OD, bottom boss standoff height (thrust face).
   COSMETIC / SECONDARY - round these off: pocket outer radius and depth, spoke rib thickness, chamfers and fillets, hub top rim detail.
4. A PRINTED REPLACEMENT IS NOT A CREPT 20-YEAR-OLD MOULDING. It starts at nominal, in a different material with different stiffness and creep behaviour. Copying worn geometry exactly is not automatically right - say so if a measured value looks like wear rather than design intent. The groove is the obvious candidate, since that is where the cord has been running.
notes:
FINAL AUTHORITATIVE DIMENSION SET (Paul, 2026-10-28, refined). Supersedes the description's measurement 2, the 'DATUM CORRECTION' note and the 'THIRD READING' note.
Paul: 'go with 2.2 and 5.66' then corrected to 'or 5.68'. Use 5.68 - it is the exact complement of 2.20 against the 7.88 hub height; 5.66 was a rounding.

PARAMETERISE IT THIS WAY. The web thickness is the single driven parameter; BOTH depths are DERIVED. Do not hardcode the depths as independent constants - that is how these numbers drifted apart in the first place.

  web_t (pocket floor height above the bottom face) = 2.20   <-- THE PARAMETER
  pocket depth from the raised hub top (7.88)  = 7.88 - web_t = 5.68   (derived)
  pocket depth from the outer flange face (6.5) = 6.50 - web_t = 4.30   (derived)

Add an assert that web_t is positive and leaves sane material, and echo the two derived depths so they can be eyeballed against the calipers.

RETIRED - do not use: the earlier 4.48 figure, and the floor positions it implied (2.02 flange-datum / 3.40 hub-datum).
UNCHANGED and still standing: arm tip DIAMETER 19.98mm => arm tip radius 9.99mm => top flange ring (21.67-19.98)/2 = 0.845mm.

=== THE CLASH STILL STANDS - STILL THE CORE TASK ===
A flat floor at z=2.20 with the pocket outer wall at r=9.99 still falls INSIDE the groove's vertical span at that radius (z=1.55 to 4.96 for a 2.2mm-deep mid-plane half-round groove). Lowering the floor from 3.40 to 2.20 does not help; it sits deeper into the groove's span.
Resolution must come from the groove's true profile and axial position - cad-critic finding 4 (real groove is a V with a radiused root, ~2.2mm wide at half depth vs 3.25 modelled) and finding 3 / openscad-03d (groove centre ~0.55mm below mid-plane). Derive both from the broken cross-sections IMG_0974/0975/0976.

=== IN-FLIGHT PASS IS STALE ===
cad-designer was launched with floor z=3.40 / web 3.40mm. Correct values are 2.20 / 2.20. Check its output against this set on return; it will likely need superseding rather than accepting.

title: Critic review: Lamona pulley wheel render vs source photos (openscad-ycm)
description:
Independent adversarial review of the model produced for design issue openscad-ycm.

Renders:
- output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm-render.png (3/4 from above)
- output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm-underside.png (underside)

Source photos: source/lamona_pulley_wheel/images/ (IMG_0966 top, IMG_0967 bottom, IMG_0968 side profile, IMG_0965 mount)
Spec: source/lamona_pulley_wheel/requirements.md

Scope: form, proportion and fidelity to the photos/spec ONLY. Not printability, tolerances or material - those belong to cad-designer.

NOTE: the designer pre-emptively predicted the critic would flag the top pocket band as too narrow and the top flange as too wide. That prediction is deliberately NOT being passed to cad-critic, to preserve the independence of the review. Reconcile the critic's findings against openscad-d3l when recording them.
notes:
CAD-CRITIC REVIEW (one pass, 2026-10-28). Inputs: render + underside render, IMG_0966/0967/0968,
requirements.md + human clarifications (all three key figures = diameters; 6 arms at 60; 6 top pockets).

METHOD: calibrated IMG_0966 (top) and IMG_0968 (side) against the known OD 21.67 mm and extracted
silhouette/radial measurements numerically. Side view established as near-zero camera tilt
(hub height reads 7.94 mm vs spec 7.88), so side-profile readings are trustworthy.

WHAT MATCHES (confirmed, no change needed):
- OD 21.67, hub boss OD 10.30 (photo reads 10.5-10.7), bore 6.04 (photo 5.7-6.3 incl. chamfer).
- Hub height 7.88 (photo 7.94). Wheel thickness 6.5 (photo 6.5-6.6 once the top-edge radius is allowed for).
- Six arms at 60 deg, six pockets: count and spacing correct.
- Groove DEPTH 2.2 mm: photo reads 2.23 mm. Groove mouth height 3.5 mm: photo 3.63 mm. Root radius ~1.75-1.8. Good.
- Bottom features PROTRUDE below the bottom face (model's boss reading is correct - IMG_0968 shows
  them clearly standing proud). Size 1.8 (photo 1.5-1.9 h, 1.6-2.3 w). Centre radius 8.365
  (side view gives 8.34). Diametrically opposed (bottom view gives 180.7 deg). All good.
- Overall silhouette reads as the right object.

FINDING 1 - MAJOR - top pockets too small in radius / top flange ring ~2x too wide.
Measured in IMG_0966 from two independent quadrants: the arm tips and the pocket outer wall both
sit at r = 9.3-9.5 mm (D ~18.6-19.0). Model pocket_or = 7.835 (D 15.67). Real top flange annulus is
~1.4 mm wide; model's is 3.0 mm. Render reads as a heavy flange ring with a small opening; photo
reads as a thin rim with large open sectors. ~22% radial shortfall on the arms.

FINDING 2 - MAJOR, COUPLED TO 1 - pockets far too deep / web far too thin.
Model floor z=1.5 => 5.0 mm deep pockets. The real part cannot be built that way: a pocket at
r=9.4 would break into the groove (root r=8.635) unless its floor sits ABOVE the groove's upper
shoulder (z~4.45). So real pocket depth is ~2.0-2.2 mm over a ~4.4 mm solid web. This is why the
model had to pull pocket_or in to 7.835 to keep rim_wall - the two errors are the same error.
In the render the arms read as tall chunky blocks in a deep well; in the photo they are shallow
thin ribs on a near-solid face.

FINDING 3 - MODERATE - groove is off-centre in the real part, symmetric in the model.
Photo: top flange ~2.05 mm, groove 3.63 mm, bottom lip ~0.90 mm; groove centre sits ~0.55-0.6 mm
BELOW the wheel mid-plane. Model: 1.50 / 3.50 / 1.50, centred. Side silhouette of the real part
reads top-heavy (thick upper shoulder, thin lower lip); the render reads symmetric.

FINDING 4 - MODERATE, LOWER CONFIDENCE - groove cross-section too open.
Depth, mouth height and root radius all match, but the real flanks are steeper. At half depth
(1.12 mm) the real groove is ~2.2 mm wide vs the model's 3.25 mm. Real = V with a radiused root;
model = half-round channel. Render shows a broad rounded belly the photo does not have.
Caveat: measured near the groove mouth where photographic bloom is worst.

FINDING 5 - MINOR - arm ribs ~30-50% too thick. Photo ~0.7-1.0 mm; model spoke_t = 1.30.

FINDING 6 - MINOR COSMETIC - hub boss top rim is scalloped in the render: the six spokes punch
through the hub's top chamfer leaving six square tabs around the hub's upper edge. The real hub
rim is a clean continuous circle (IMG_0966).

FINDING 7 - COSMETIC ONLY, NO ACTION - real bottom face carries mould markings ("5", cavity marks)
the model omits; real top outer edge has a larger radius (~0.5-0.7 mm) than the 0.40 chamfer, while
the real bottom outer edge is nearly sharp.

NOT ASSESSABLE: pocket depth could not be read directly from the photos (near-axial top view, no
3/4 photo of the real part exists in the set); Finding 2 is inferred geometrically, not measured.

Reconciliation vs openscad-d3l: the designer's self-prediction (pocket band too narrow / flange too
wide) matches Finding 1, reached independently. The designer did not predict Findings 2, 3, 4 or 6.

Review complete. One pass, no further iteration. Issue deliberately left open for the human
Design Acceptance decision per AGENTS.md. No files changed, no .scad edits, no re-render.
close_reason: Critic review delivered and recorded in notes. Core dimensions all confirmed correct (OD 21.67, hub 10.30, bore 6.04, hub height 7.88, thickness 6.5, groove depth 2.20, six arms at 60deg, protruding bottom bosses). Significant top-face proportion defects found, root-caused and reconciled onto openscad-d3l (raised P1). Moderate/minor findings filed separately. Force-closed: blocked only by openscad-ycm, which is intentionally left open for Paul's Design Acceptance decision per AGENTS.md.

title: Print setup for pulley openscad-ycm: material and support strategy
description:
The part prints axis-vertical (as modelled) on the Bambu A1, 0.4mm nozzle.

MATERIAL - do not use PLA. The original end fittings are marked >POM< (acetal). This part lives inside a dishwasher door: warm, damp, and under sustained cord tension whenever the door is held. PLA creeps under constant load and softens well below the temperatures a dishwasher door sees. Use PETG (easy, tough enough, good enough wear) or PA/PAHT-CF or ASA. 0.16mm layers, 4 perimeters, 40-60% infill - the part is small and nearly solid anyway; perimeters carry the load, not infill.

ORIENTATION / SUPPORT - the lowest features are the two 1.8mm standoff bosses, so as modelled the wheel stands on two 1.8mm squares with the full Ø21.67mm bottom face bridging 1.8mm above the bed. Two options:
 (a) print as modelled with supports on build plate only and a brim; the support column under the bottom face is only 1.8mm tall so it is trivial for the slicer, and the bottom face is a thrust face whose finish barely matters because the bosses carry the load. This is the recommended route.
 (b) print the bosses-up (flip in the slicer) and glue the part down on its flat bottom face - no support at all, bosses print as clean 1.8mm towers on a solid face - but then the groove and spokes are unchanged and the HUB BOSS ends up on the bed, which is wrong. Do not do this; (a) is correct.

GROOVE OVERHANG - the lower half of the torus groove is a taper inward and prints cleanly. The upper half is a circular overhang that starts horizontal at the groove root (z=3.25mm) and steepens to vertical by z=4.95mm. This is the classic pulley-groove overhang: expect a small droop in the first few layers above the root. It is circumferential and self-supporting enough to leave unsupported; if the first print shows a lip that catches the cord, dress it with a round file or enable supports in that band only.

OTHER - add a 0.1-0.2mm hole-compensation or verify the bore on a test print before fitting (see the bore/stud bead). Expect elephant's foot on the two boss feet; a 0.1mm first-layer squish compensation or a light deburr will keep them bearing flat.
acceptance_criteria: Part printed in a non-PLA material, spins freely on the stud, cord seats in the groove without catching.

title: Pulley pocket outer radius compromised for FDM minimum wall
description:
Fidelity-vs-printability tradeoff made during openscad-ycm, flagged for the critic.

Overlaying reference circles on IMG_0966 puts the outer wall of the top pocket at roughly r = 8.6mm - which is also the groove root radius. Reproducing that literally leaves ZERO material between the pocket wall and the groove root at the groove's deepest point: the pockets would break through into the groove all the way round, and the cord would catch.

The moulded original must therefore have ~0.5mm there and I am over-reading the photo. The model derives pocket_or = groove_root_r - rim_wall with rim_wall = 0.80mm, two perimeters at a 0.4mm nozzle, which is the floor for FDM. That pulls the pocket outer radius in to 7.835mm.

Visible effect in the render: the pocket/spoke band is narrower and the top flange annulus wider than in IMG_0966. cad-critic will likely flag this as a proportion mismatch - it is deliberate. rim_wall is a single parameter; do not reduce it below 0.8.
acceptance_criteria: Human/critic accepts the narrower pocket, or decides to accept a thinner rim wall.
notes:
CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-10-28) - supersedes my earlier reconciliation on this issue, which was WRONG.

Paul has now measured the original with calipers:
- arm tip DIAMETER 19.98mm => arm tip radius 9.99mm, top flange ring 0.845mm wide
- pocket depth 4.48mm measured from the TOP FLANGE FACE down to the POCKET FLOOR (datum confirmed by Paul) => floor at z=2.02, web beneath only ~2.02mm

So the pocket is DEEP and WIDE. cad-critic's finding 2 (shallow ~2.0-2.2mm pocket over a ~4.4mm web) had the split INVERTED and is wrong; my reconciliation built on it is wrong too. cad-critic's finding 1 (pocket radius too small, flange too wide) is confirmed and was understated - real flange is 0.845mm, not the ~1.4mm the critic estimated, against 3.0mm in the model.

cad-designer's instinct that a deep pocket at a large radius clashes with the groove was therefore CORRECT - but its response (pull the radius in to 7.835 and call it a deliberate min-wall compromise) is still wrong, because the real part demonstrably has both. Resolving how the real part closes that geometry is the core task of the revision issue openscad-l7n, to be worked out from the new broken cross-section photos IMG_0973-0977.

Superseded by openscad-l7n.

title: Design replacement pulley wheel for Lamona LAM8652 dishwasher door mechanism
description:
Job folder: source/lamona_pulley_wheel/ (spec: requirements.md, photos: images/IMG_0965-0971.png).

Replacement grooved pulley wheel for the door-balance cord mechanism of a Lamona LAM8652 dishwasher. Original is broken and unobtainable. Mounts on a screw with a washer fixed to the door; must spin freely on that screw and carry a 3.15mm cord in a circumferential groove.

Stated measurements (verbatim from spec):
- External diameter 21.67mm
- Internal axle hole radius 6.04mm
- Axle outer radius 10.30mm
- Five spokes (spec notes it is unsure whether cosmetic or functional)
- Circumferential groove (torus cut) for 3.15mm cord, cord should sit flush
- Wheel thickness 6.5mm; internal axle (hub) width 7.88mm, spokes rise to meet the raised hub height
- Bottom face: two square notches 1.8mm height/width/depth, 16.73mm apart

Photo index: IMG_0966 top, IMG_0967 bottom (notches), IMG_0968 side profile, IMG_0969/0970 cord mechanism, IMG_0965 screw+washer mount, IMG_0971 model plate.

OPEN AMBIGUITIES - do not silently resolve, flag them in the handoff:
1. Radius/diameter inconsistency. OD 21.67mm with an 'axle outer radius' of 10.30mm leaves only ~0.5mm of rim outside the hub, which contradicts the photos. Likewise an axle hole 'radius' of 6.04mm (Ø12.08) would be wider than the hub itself. The two inner figures look like they may be diameters, but that is the human's call.
2. Spoke count: spec says five; the top-down photo does not obviously agree. Confirm against IMG_0966 rather than assuming.
3. Spoke function: spec explicitly asks whether the spokes are structural or cosmetic.

Deliverables per AGENTS.md File Naming: output/lamona_pulley_wheel-<this-issue-id>.scad and .stl (no .step - OpenSCAD 2021.01 cannot export it), plus a rendered PNG for cad-critic review. Read printer.yaml before making manufacturing decisions (Bambu Lab A1 FDM). Parameterise all dimensions.
notes:
HUMAN RESOLUTION 1 (Paul, 2026-10-28): inner measurements are DIAMETERS, not radii. requirements.md corrected by Paul.
- Bore = 6.04mm DIAMETER
- Axle/hub boss outer = 10.30mm DIAMETER
- Wheel = 21.67mm outer diameter
Ambiguity 1 CLOSED.

HUMAN RESOLUTION 2 (Paul, 2026-10-28, confirmed): spoke count is NOT five. Geometry is three ribs lying on three diameters that cross at the centre; the central axle boss and its bore interrupt them. Each rib is therefore physically two arms running from the boss OD out to the rim.
=> MODEL AS SIX ARMS, EVENLY SPACED AT 60 DEGREES.
'Three' counts ribs, 'six' counts arms.
requirements.md says 'three spokes' but does not capture the crossing/interrupted detail - this note is authoritative on arm count and spacing.
Ambiguity 2 CLOSED.

AMBIGUITY 3 (spokes structural vs cosmetic) still OPEN - designer to assess and report.

HUMAN RESOLUTION 4 (Paul, 2026-10-28): the six wedge features on the TOP face are option (b) - RECESSED WEDGE-SHAPED POCKETS. The six sectors BETWEEN the arms are recessed below the top face; the wedges are voids, not added material. The arms and the raised axle boss stand proud of these pockets.
NOT recorded in requirements.md - Paul confirmed this verbally only; this note is the sole record.
Still to determine (designer to derive from images/IMG_0966.png plus the 6.5mm wheel thickness / 7.88mm hub width relationship, and REPORT the assumption rather than bury it): whether each pocket spans the full 60deg sector between adjacent arms, the pocket floor depth relative to the top of the arms, and the corner radii of the pockets.
Ambiguity 4 geometry type CLOSED; dimensions OPEN.

IMPACT: the in-flight cad-designer pass (briefed with 'five spokes', radius/diameter unresolved, no wedge pockets) will be stale on spoke geometry and missing feature 4. Plan: let it finish for its groove/hub/notch/printability work, then raise a NEW design issue carrying the corrected diameters, 6-arm-at-60deg geometry and the recessed wedge pockets, and run the critic pass against that model. Do not reopen or overwrite this issue's outputs (AGENTS.md File Naming: new issue id => new output filenames).

title: DECISION ONLY: lamona_pulley_wheel design ready for review
description:
Design issue openscad-ycm. Critic review openscad-ca8 (closed).

RENDERS:
- output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm-render.png (3/4 from above)
- output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm-underside.png
Source: output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm.scad / .stl

HEADLINE: proportions are WRONG on the top face. Everything else matches the real part well.

THE MISMATCH (critic findings 1+2, which are one defect):
The six top pockets are both too small in radius and far too deep. Real part has arm tips and pocket outer wall at r=9.3-9.5mm; the model has 7.835mm. That leaves the model with a 3.0mm flange ring where the real part has ~1.4mm, and arms ~22% short. The render reads as a heavy ring around a small opening with chunky blocks in a deep well; the photo shows a thin rim, large open sectors and shallow thin ribs on a near-solid face.

ROOT CAUSE - and the designer got this wrong: it floored the pocket at z=1.5 (5.0mm deep in a 6.5mm wheel), which WOULD break into the groove at the correct radius, so it pulled the radius in and recorded the result as a 'deliberate' FDM min-wall compromise (openscad-d3l). The critic, reviewing independently without being told that, found the real answer: the pocket is SHALLOW on the real part (~2.0-2.2mm over a ~4.4mm solid web, floor above the groove shoulder). Fix the depth and the radius conflict disappears entirely. No min-wall compromise is actually needed. openscad-d3l raised P3 -> P1.

CRITIC CAVEAT, worth your attention: that pocket depth is INFERRED geometrically, not measured - there is no 3/4 photo of the real part in the set. You still have the broken original. A caliper reading of POCKET DEPTH and ARM-TIP RADIUS would settle it cheaply and de-risk the rework.

WHAT MATCHES (confirmed by measurement against the photos):
OD 21.67, hub boss 10.30, bore 6.04, hub height 7.88 (photo 7.94), wheel thickness 6.5, groove depth 2.20 (photo 2.23), groove mouth 3.50 (photo 3.63), six arms at 60deg, and the bottom features correctly modelled as protruding bosses.

ALSO OPEN:
- openscad-03d (P2) groove sits ~0.55mm below mid-plane on the real part, symmetric in the model
- openscad-ajg (P3) spoke ribs 30-50% too thick; hub top rim scalloped where spokes punch through the chamfer
- openscad-6ac (P2) confirm the bottom bosses are thrust standoffs
- openscad-cy3 (P1) print setup - NOT PLA, original is marked >POM<; use PETG/ASA/PA in a warm damp dishwasher door under sustained cord tension

RESOLVED THIS CYCLE:
- openscad-so3 CLOSED - you confirmed the cord is not flush; 2.2mm groove is correct, spec reworded, IMG_0972 added
- openscad-vim P1 -> P3 - stud will not be measured (needs dishwasher disassembly); accepted risk, bore is a one-line parametric change (bore_print_comp, line 80) plus a reprint

title: Groove is off-centre on the real part, symmetric in the model
description:
cad-critic finding 3 (from openscad-ca8; discovered-from openscad-ycm), measured off IMG_0968 which is a near-zero-tilt true elevation.

Real part: top flange ~2.05mm, groove 3.63mm, bottom lip ~0.90mm. Groove centre sits ~0.55-0.6mm BELOW the wheel mid-plane, so the silhouette reads top-heavy (thick upper shoulder, thin lower lip).
Model: 1.50 / 3.50 / 1.50, groove centred on the mid-plane.

Likely functional rather than cosmetic: the upper flange is the one the cord loads against, and per the designer the spokes exist to brace it. Worth understanding before 'fixing'.

Fix is a groove z-offset parameter. Do not action without a human decision.

comments.author: Paul Ryan
comments.text: critic finding is on the money, the groove is offset.

title: Pulley bottom features are bosses, not notches - confirm their function
description:
requirements.md calls them 'two square notches of 1.8mm height, width and depth, 16.73mm apart'. A notch is normally a recess; these stand PROUD.

Evidence: the IMG_0968 silhouette shows the bottom face at x~1445px with a square feature reaching out to x~1386px, i.e. ~1.4mm clear of the bottom face. IMG_0967 shows them catching the light with their own cast shadows. Measured radius from the axis ~7.9mm against the stated 8.365mm (16.73/2), consistent allowing for camera tilt.

Modelled as bosses. notch_protrudes = false switches them to recesses in one line.

Open question for the human: these are almost certainly thrust standoffs, holding the spinning wheel off the door bracket face on two small pads instead of a full Ø21.67mm face, to cut friction. If so they are functional and must be kept. Two square-edged pads is an odd choice though (they will dig in rather than slide), so they could instead be moulding/ejector artefacts. Confirm by looking at the bracket face for two matching wear marks.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed whether the bottom squares protrude (standoffs) or recess, and whether they are functional.

title: Groove depth: photo says 2.2mm, spec says cord should sit flush
description:
requirements.md asks for a torus-cut groove 'for the chord to fit flush'. If 'flush' means the cord's outer surface sits level with the 21.67mm OD, the groove would need to be ~3.3mm deep. The original is not that deep.

Measured from the IMG_0968 silhouette (surface of revolution, so the silhouette IS the radius profile): flange diameter 21.5-21.6mm, groove root diameter 17.2-17.4mm, groove mouth ~3.3mm wide axially. That gives a groove depth of ~2.2mm.

The model uses groove_depth = 2.20 with a torus arc radius of 1.75mm (cord radius 1.575 + 0.175 clearance). Two independent checks agree with this:
 - a 1.75mm arc centred on the 6.5mm disc mid-plane leaves exactly 1.50mm of flange above and below, matching the uniform ~1.5mm moulded wall seen elsewhere in the part;
 - the resulting groove mouth is 3.38mm wide, matching the 3.3mm measured off the photo.

Consequence: the 3.15mm cord nests ~70% into the groove and stands 0.95mm proud of the flanges (pitch diameter 20.42mm). That is normal for a cord pulley and is what the original did, so I kept it.

To take the literal 'flush' reading instead, set groove_depth = 3.33. That drops the groove root to Ø15.4mm and would force rim_wall and the pocket geometry to be reworked - do not change it without also rechecking the asserts.
acceptance_criteria: Human confirms the groove reproduces the original (cord proud by ~1mm) rather than burying the cord flush with the OD.
notes:
HUMAN RESOLUTION (Paul, 2026-10-28): confirmed the cord is NOT flush with the wheel OD on the real part. cad-designer's measured groove depth of 2.2mm (cord nesting ~70%, standing ~0.95mm proud) is therefore CORRECT and matches the original.

requirements.md line 19 updated by Paul from 'to fit flush' to 'to fit almost flush', and now references a new photo IMG_0972.png showing the cord seated in the original wheel.

No change required to the model. Do NOT rework the rim to achieve a literal flush fit (groove_depth=3.33); the as-built 2.2mm is right.

NOTE: IMG_0972.png was added AFTER cad-critic was briefed on openscad-ca8, so the critic did not see it. Its brief listed IMG_0965-0970 only. If the critic's findings turn on groove depth or cord seating, weigh them against this resolution rather than treating them as new defects.
close_reason: Resolved by human: Paul confirmed the cord is not flush on the real part, so the measured 2.2mm groove depth is correct as modelled. Spec reworded to 'almost flush' and IMG_0972.png added as evidence. No model change needed.

title: Decide spoke count for pulley: spec says 5, photo analysis says 6
description:
requirements.md states five spokes. Measured evidence says six.

Method: sampled the brightness of IMG_0966 around concentric rings centred on the bore and took the angular FFT after removing the lighting gradient. Across radii 5.4-9.1mm the 6th harmonic dominates (amplitude 5.4 falling to 0.4) while the 5th harmonic never rises above 1.9. A polar unwrap of the same photo shows six evenly spaced ribs at 60 deg.

The model uses spoke_count = 6. Change that one line to 5 to follow the written spec.

Related question the spec asks - are they structural or cosmetic? Assessment: structural, but secondary. The primary load path from the grooved rim to the hub is the continuous 1.5mm bottom web. The spokes brace the upper groove flange, which is otherwise carried only by a ~0.8mm annular ledge standing ~5mm proud of that web, against the cord's side load. In the injection-moulded original they also exist to keep wall thickness uniform and avoid sink marks on a 6.5mm solid disc - a concern that does not apply to FDM. The .scad has solid_web = false; setting it true omits pocket and spokes entirely and prints a solid disc, which would be stronger and is a legitimate option if the human does not care about matching the original's appearance.
acceptance_criteria: Human confirms 5 vs 6 spokes and whether to keep the moulded web/pocket form or print solid.

title: Redesign cable clip for secure desk attachment
description: Redesign the cable clip to properly attach to a 3mm desk edge without screws or adhesive. The new design must use mechanical interference-fit geometry to prevent falling off under its own weight, allow deliberate installation/removal, retain a 5mm cable separately from the desk attachment mechanism, and allow cable insertion without threading through a closed hole.
acceptance_criteria:
• Mechanically attaches to 3mm desk edge without screws, adhesive or separate hardware
• Uses clip/hook/interference-fit geometry that prevents falling off under its own weight
• Allows deliberate installation and removal from desk edge
• Retains 5mm cable separately from desk attachment mechanism
• Allows cable insertion without threading through closed hole
• Has approximately 0.3mm clearance around 3mm desk edge
• Maintains at least 2mm wall thickness
• Requires no supports when printed on configured Bambu A1

description: Create a parametric OpenSCAD cable clip that attaches to 3mm thick desk/shelf and holds 5mm diameter cables. Requirements: 25mm wide, 20mm deep, 15mm high, 2mm minimum wall thickness, 5.5mm cable opening, 0.3mm clearance around desk edge, no supports required.

title: Spoke ribs too thick; hub top rim scalloped by spokes
description:
Two minor cad-critic findings (from openscad-ca8; discovered-from openscad-ycm).

Finding 5: arm ribs measure ~0.7-1.0mm on the real part (IMG_0966) vs spoke_t = 1.30 in the model - 30-50% too thick. Contributes to the overall 'chunky' read but is secondary to the pocket depth defect (openscad-d3l). Note FDM minimum wall when correcting: 0.8mm is two perimeters at a 0.4mm nozzle, so there is limited room to thin these.

Finding 6: the six spokes punch through the hub boss's top chamfer, leaving six square tabs around its upper edge (visible at ~2,4,6,8,10 o'clock in the render). The real hub rim is a clean continuous circle. A modelling artefact of how the spokes are unioned to the hub, not a deliberate feature.

title: Confirm pulley bore size and stud diameter before printing openscad-ycm
description:
The pulley bore is the single fit-critical dimension and nothing in the job folder measures the stud it runs on.

Spec says 'internal axle hole radius 6.04mm'. The model reads it as a DIAMETER (overlaying a 6.04mm circle on IMG_0966 against the known 21.67mm OD lands exactly on the bore wall; a 12.08mm bore is impossible since the hub boss is only 10.30mm across). bore_d = 6.04 in output/lamona_pulley_wheel-openscad-ycm.scad.

Unresolved: IMG_0965 shows the stud with a push-on star washer but gives no scale, so the running clearance is unknown. 6.04 was the moulded bore of a part that already had the right clearance, so it is probably fine - but if the stud is close to 6mm the printed wheel will bind.

Action for the human: caliper the stud shank, then set bore_d so the FINISHED hole clears it by at least 0.3mm on diameter. bore_print_comp (0.30) already opens the modelled hole to 6.34mm to compensate for FDM holes printing undersize; verify on the first print and adjust.
acceptance_criteria: Stud diameter measured; bore_d/bore_print_comp set so the printed wheel spins freely on the stud with no detectable bind.
notes:
HUMAN DECISION (Paul, 2026-10-28): the stud will NOT be measured. Doing so needs partial disassembly of the dishwasher - a two-person job the repairers did - and Paul does not want to take that on.

ACCEPTED RISK with mitigation: the .scad is properly parametric, so a bad bore is a one-line change and a reprint. Verified by orchestrator:
- line 22: bore_d = 6.04
- line 80: bore_print_comp = 0.30
- line 94: bore_r = (bore_d + bore_print_comp) / 2
Nothing else in the file hardcodes the bore.

Risk is LOWER than the designer's handoff implied: 6.04mm is the measured bore of the ORIGINAL wheel, which already fitted the stud correctly. We are copying a known-good dimension, not guessing at the stud. The only real unknown is FDM hole shrinkage, which bore_print_comp exists to absorb.

REFRAMED from 'measure the stud before printing' to a print-time fit check: print the wheel, offer it to the stud, and if it binds or is sloppy adjust bore_print_comp (not bore_d - bore_d records the original part's measurement) and reprint. Downgraded P1 -> P3; no longer a blocker on design acceptance.

Optional cheaper iteration: print a small test coupon with a range of bore diameters rather than full wheels. Not actioned - the wheel is small enough that a straight reprint is likely simpler.
